summary: Fixed in #710 (60633eff3), which is also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3. The shared rpc client (web, desktop, mobile, hosted relay) subscribes with replay:"metadata". The server answers with history-free started events marked replay:true, and bootstrap events no longer count against the 4 MiB budget. A mounted drawer that receives a replay showing missed output now re-hydrates through terminal.open({sinceCursor}), which returns only the delta from the history cursor index. It no longer blanks the view. A cached or detached view refuses buffer catch-up when a replay is pending and opens with its own cursor. The store only registers replayed terminals and never opens them, and persist writes are skipped when the persisted slice is unchanged. Old and new clients and servers stay compatible in both directions: the old payload was Schema.Struct({}), excess fields are ignored, and replay is opt-in. I tried to break the reconnect, first-mount race, cached-view and failure paths and found no defect. Two residual history/bandwidth paths remain. Both are outside this finding's connect-time scope.

evidence.note: This is the only caller of subscribeTerminalEvents (git grep). It always passes { replay: "metadata" }, so it covers web, desktop, mobile and hosted relay (relay/transport.ts:45 passes through).
terminalBootstrapEvent sets history to "", replay:true and hasRunningSubprocess for metadata subscribers. Legacy callers keep the full snapshot.

Bootstrap is built from running sessions and concatenated without being queued, so it is not charged against the budget. The live cursor filter is unchanged from f1be4abc7. Generation is per manager lifetime (contracts terminal.ts:42), so the filter does not drop events after a restart.
The payload is TerminalSubscribeEventsInput. At f1be4abc7 it was Schema.Struct({}), so an old server ignores replay and old clients still get full snapshots.
openSnapshot returns the history after sinceCursor through TerminalHistoryCursorIndex.since (historyCursorIndex.ts:74-92). It falls back to full history on a generation mismatch, trimming or reset.
appliedCursor is not advanced for replays. An accepted replay sets terminalHydratedRef=false and calls openTerminal({resync:true}) without writing the empty snapshot.
applyPendingTerminalEvents stops at a replay. openTerminal sends sinceCursor=appliedCursor, appends the delta, replays buffered entries after the answer's cursor, and on failure resumes live events.
resolveTerminalViewCatchUp returns null when the pending buffer has a replay, so a reattached view goes through the sinceCursor open and never applies output on top of a gap.
A replay is accepted only for a later cursor or a new generation. Otherwise the store and drawer drop it and keep the scrollback.
For replays, registerThreadTerminal never opens or focuses and is reference-preserving, so terminalStateByThreadKey is unchanged and no persist write happens.
skipUnchangedPersistedState wraps createJSONStorage, so the JSON.stringify and setItem are skipped when the partialized reference is unchanged.
Browser tests cover a caught-up replay that keeps the scrollback and a missed replay that re-hydrates from the view's cursor. ThreadTerminalDrawer.browser.tsx:477 covers the detached-view replay.

Residual, out of scope: a project-script run calls terminal.open on a possibly long-lived base terminal and throws away the full history it returns. The drawer it opens then fetches the history again unless its view is cached.

Residual, out of scope: mobile (and hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:288) sets applyTerminalEvent to a no-op, but connection.ts:320 still subscribes unconditionally. Connect-time history is gone, but live output of every terminal still streams to the phone and is dropped.

fixDefects: None found. I checked reconnect with missed output, reconnect without missed output, a first mount racing the subscription, a cached view with a buffered replay, a failed resync open, cross-generation replays and wire compatibility in both directions. Each one is handled correctly. Non-defect residuals: (1) useChatProjectScripts.ts:162 downloads and discards up to 2 MiB of history per script run on a non-busy base terminal, and the opened drawer may then fetch it again. (2) mobile subscribes to terminal events it discards (environmentDriver.ts:519, hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:288 with connection.ts:320), so live terminal output of all threads still crosses the relay to phones. Both are outside this finding's connect/reconnect-history scope.
implementationSketch: Nothing is required for this finding. Optional follow-ups for the residuals: (a) project scripts: in useChatProjectScripts.runProjectScript, pass sinceCursor set to the store's reconciliation cursor for the target terminal (terminalEventReconciliationByKey[key].cursor). An existing live session then answers with a near-empty delta, and a new or restarted one still returns the full history. Alternatively, add an explicit includeHistory:false to TerminalOpenInput and honor it in Manager.open/openSnapshot. Test: a Manager.test case where an open with the current cursor returns history "", plus a unit test for runProjectScript asserting sinceCursor. (b) mobile: make applyTerminalEvent optional in the createEnvironmentConnection input (connection.ts:57), skip input.client.terminal.onEvent when it is absent, and drop the no-op from both mobile call sites. Test: a connection.test asserting that no subscribeTerminalEvents stream opens without applyTerminalEvent.
